sources.author_assertions:
## Summary

Fix cached prompt continuation in `FLAGenerationMixin`: honor the upstream sequence-length protocol, retain first-pass embeddings, and avoid truncating an already-sliced prompt or reusing stale embeddings during decoding. Preserve the legacy cache-position protocol, consolidate input assembly, and place cached dependency checks in `fla.utils.env` without requiring Transformers for core-only imports.

Fixes #1281. Supersedes #1445 with current-main validation and expanded regression coverage; the original contribution from #1282 is preserved in the commit history. This shared fix affects models inheriting `FLAGenerationMixin`; CAT keeps its separate implementation, and YOCO forwards the new optional arguments through its existing override. Model configurations, checkpoint keys, kernels, dtypes, and numerical tolerances are unchanged.

## Test plan

Baseline: `8e7bcf382`; candidate: `90a18fb236ddbe92c5744edb5b152ebfcabb984b`.

The parameterized tests cover cached IDs/embeddings, empty or missing IDs, already-sliced prompts, empty/populated/absent caches, stale embeddings during decoding, and legacy cache-position handling. Modern input tensors are also compared against upstream `GenerationMixin`. Import coverage verifies that the common utilities remain usable without importing Transformers.

Host commands use `FLA_CI_ENV=0 python -m pytest ... -q` with Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130.msh in isolated dependency environments:

| Transformers | Test selection | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4.52.4 | `tests/models/test_generation_utils.py tests/test_utils.py tests/utils/test_import.py` | 43 passed, 3 skipped |
| 4.57.1 | Above plus `tests/test_public_api.py tests/models/test_hybrid_attention.py` | 290 passed, 5 skipped |
| 5.6.2 | Generation and utility/import tests above | 44 passed, 2 skipped |
| 5.20.1 | Generation and utility/import tests above | 44 passed, 2 skipped |

Protocol skips select the applicable installed API; the 4.57.1 host suite also skips accelerator-only hybrid comparisons. `pre-commit run --files fla/models/utils.py fla/utils/env.py fla/utils/__init__.py tests/models/test_generation_utils.py tests/test_utils.py tests/utils/test_import.py` and `git diff --check` pass.

GPU validation on NVIDIA GB200, PyTorch 2.11.0.post1+cu132.msh, Transformers 4.57.1: `FLA_CI_ENV=0 FLA_DISABLE_BACKEND_DISPATCH=1 python -m pytest tests/models/test_generation_utils.py tests/models/test_cache.py tests/models/test_modeling_gated_deltanet.py::test_generate_prefill -q --tb=short` — **59 passed, 6 skipped**. The skips are one modern-protocol test and five legacy-cache constructor cases incompatible with the installed upstream cache base. The GatedDeltaNet regression compares actual `.generate()` results with manual greedy decoding.

The dependency finder selected 45 files; the shared-callsite audit narrows the changed execution path to generation input preparation and optional imports. The applicable host checks, cache checks, and actual generation regression above passed. The full model forward/backward and operator matrix was not rerun: this change does not modify those execution paths.

## Benchmark / NCU

Input-preparation microbenchmark against `8e7bcf382`, candidate `90a18fb2`, on the same ARM Neoverse-N1 CPU pinned to one core; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130.msh, Transformers 5.6.2. Inputs: CPU int64 IDs `[2, 64]`; cached decode has 63 past tokens. Both implementations produce identical model inputs on these workloads before timing. Each method receives 1,000 warmups, then 15 alternating rounds of 10,000 calls with GC disabled; report median wall-clock microseconds per call using `perf_counter_ns`.

| Input preparation | Baseline (µs) | Candidate (µs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Standard prefill (`next_sequence_length=None`, first iteration) | 2.461 | 2.416 |
| Explicit full-length suffix (`next_sequence_length=64`, first iteration) | 2.460 | 13.378 |
| Cached decode (`next_sequence_length=1`, subsequent iteration) | 19.446 | 19.297 |

Explicit full-length suffix preparation costs about 11 µs more because it now performs the requested tensor slice; the baseline ignores that argument. Standard prefill and cached decode remain close to the measured baseline. This is host input-preparation timing, not end-to-end generation throughput. No kernel changed; dense/varlen kernel benchmarks and NCU are inapplicable.

## Breaking changes

None. Existing argument order, defaults, imports, model checkpoints, and supported legacy generation protocols remain available. The two upstream generation arguments are optional.

- [x] Kernel changes include same-hardware before/after benchmark numbers, dense + varlen where applicable (tick as N/A when no kernel code changed).
- [ ] This PR is minor/cosmetic-only (typo, formatting, style-only tweaks) — tick only if it is, and justify below.
- [ ] I understand this PR exceeds 500 changed lines and have explained its single purpose and why it should stay together below.

sources.author_assertions:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway tests that reuse a Vitest worker retain prior files' module graphs, growing memory with the file count. Separately, the process-wide worker-pool registry keeps abandoned pools and their options alive until an explicit close.

## User Impact

Abandoned pools can be collected after their callers and native resources release them. Shared-worker Gateway tests use less memory on Bun and Node. Active worker resource cleanup and failed SQLite custody remain owned by their existing lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Bucket 1 — production owner:** replace the strong worker-pool discovery set with weak registrations. Sweep collected entries during registration, close, and resource broadcast; preserve duplicate registration and failed-close behavior. Live workers retain their pools independently through their native custody and worker tracking.
- **Bucket 2 — test lifecycle:** extend the existing source-aware SQLite retirement family to reader, WAL, device-pairing, and state-publication registrations. Retire only evaluated source generations after drainage. Retire the plugin observation cache with its publication bus so the next generation reinstalls its subscriber. Preserve the shared resource map and failed-custody guard.

The new regressions fail on the original defects: an unused real pool retains its captured options, and reader registrations grow from 13 to 15 across files. The latter also checks real plugin-state commits, cache updates/deletion, and old versus current WAL listeners. No per-test cleanup hacks, Bun skips, timeout changes, or CI chunking changes.

## Evidence

One 32 GB Linux host, one shared main worker, archived file order, native-callback GC after full runner cleanup. Node v24.19.0 and checksum-verified repository Bun pin `1.4.3-canary.1+c45839085` were used throughout; the launcher-local older fork was not used for the comparison.

| 30-main-file comparison | Original heap, first → last | Fixed heap, first → last | Original → fixed OLS slope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bun | 375.14 → 1868.08 MiB | 376.69 → 1087.44 MiB | 50.498 → 22.845 MiB/file |
| Node | 658.43 → 1755.62 MiB | 662.01 → 1264.02 MiB | 35.626 → 18.409 MiB/file |

Both final runs passed **31 files / 567 tests** (the native fixture has a separate worker; the remaining 30 files share one worker). Bun: 962.38 s test duration / 965.85 s measurement; Node: 1538.47 s / 1542.32 s. OLS heap growth fell 54.8% on Bun and 48.3% on Node. These are retained-heap comparisons, not a throughput benchmark or full-shard qualification.

Six-file Bun ablations show overlapping retention roots: control 58.090 MiB/file, weak pools alone 58.453, source retirement alone 57.953, both 49.230. The combined fix was then validated over the full 30-file sample above. Individual ablations are short diagnostics, not full qualification.

The initial wake/plugin-loader/MCP/fake-timer leads were dropped. Clearing those together gave 60.545 MiB/file over three files and added no useful improvement to registry cleanup (32.949 versus 33.181). They were not promoted to further Node trials. The two retained fixes share the same long-run comparison because neither independently releases all overlapping roots.

| Lead | Decision | Bun slope evidence, MiB/file | Node slope evidence, MiB/file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Worker-pool discovery | Kept with source retirement | Alone: 58.090 → 58.453 (6 files); combined: 50.498 → 22.845 (30) | Combined: 35.626 → 18.409 (30) |
| Reader/WAL/device/publication registrations | Kept with weak pools | Alone: 58.090 → 57.953 (6); combined as above | Combined as above |
| Session-event wake globals | Dropped | Grouped original-lead screen: 60.545 (3); no additive benefit | Not screened |
| Plugin lifecycle loader promises | Dropped | Same grouped screen | Not screened |
| MCP AsyncLocalStorage snapshots | Dropped | Same grouped screen | Not screened |
| Fake-timer AsyncResource snapshots | Dropped | Same grouped screen | Not screened |

The original-lead screen grouped candidates; it does not assign independent slopes to the four dropped leads. Pool/source-retirement gains are reported jointly because the retained graphs have overlapping roots.

Two matched Bun heap-snapshot diffs support the reduction: control files 1→6 add 724,474 Functions and 45,613 Modules; fixed files 1→6 add 608,407 and 38,851. Retired reader/WAL/device publication roots disappear, while worker-pool discovery uses weak references. The bounded forward searches from the pool registry did not reach the selected named module functions in either snapshot, so they are not evidence of a removed pool-to-function path; the real abandoned-pool collection regression supplies that owner-boundary proof. Snapshot reachability does not establish exclusive ownership or retained size. Remaining graph retention is explicitly outside this patch's claims.

An initial snapshot-heavy Bun run exhausted the 16 GiB temporary filesystem's worktree safety reserve. Its worktree failures were infrastructure failures and it is not counted as passing proof. Completed snapshots were moved to persistent storage, then the Bun run was repeated without snapshot capture. No product checks or timeouts were relaxed.

Focused commands, each passing with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, with the fork first on `PATH` and a short `TMPDIR`:

```sh
pnpm test src/infra/lifecycle-tail-retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test test/non-isolated-runner.sqlite.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test test/non-isolated-runner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/infra/worker-task-pool.owned.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/infra/worker-task-pool.retained.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/infra/agent-database-readers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The memory driver preserved the archived order, one main worker, and full native-callback GC after runner cleanup. Exact final driver calls:

```sh
RETAIN_SNAPSHOTS='' RETAIN_CANDIDATE=control BUNMEM_SKIP_NATIVE=0 BUNMEM_LIMIT=31 BUNMEM_VARIANT=bun-gc BUNMEM_TIMEOUT=2400 python3 /tmp/oc-retain/measure-cleanup.py clean31-combined-bun
RETAIN_SNAPSHOTS='' RETAIN_CANDIDATE=control BUNMEM_SKIP_NATIVE=0 BUNMEM_LIMIT=31 BUNMEM_VARIANT=node-gc BUNMEM_TIMEOUT=2400 python3 /tmp/oc-retain/measure-cleanup.py final31-combined-node
```

The driver invokes `bun scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config .tmp/oc-bunmem/postcleanup.config.ts --maxWorkers=1` or `node --import tsx scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config .tmp/oc-bunmem/postcleanup.config.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the pinned include/order lists and runtime environment. Probe scripts, order, raw samples, commands, test results and snapshot analyses were retained as task evidence.

The changed retention file has 3 tests; the SQLite runner has 1 parent test exercising 21 nested tests, including its existing intentional skip and failed-teardown fixture.

Format, scoped core/root-test lint, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and both `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json` typechecks pass. Pr-simplify and independent Codex autoreview through P2 are complete, with no actionable findings.

Exact-head [CI run 39031047217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39031047217) completed successfully for `aaae0f64b6d4cd4b836d9bb74c37dc2abd7f95a4`. The bounded watcher returned GREEN with no current failed or pending checks; older superseded statuses were excluded.

Production LOC: **+26/-8 (net +18)**; test/helper LOC: **+203/-25 (net +178)**. The necessary production growth traverses/prunes weak registrations; the duplicate pool type was removed. No unrelated deletions were added to meet a line quota.
